<reason>Both sides ran disciplined, well-grounded cases and the clash progressed cleanly. PRO opened with the strongest framing (the "Buy" button asymmetry, inheritance as the default for contractual claims, the "who wrote the term" circularity charge) and pressed a genuinely hard question about why a heritable tier has never emerged. But CON did more damage in the exchange. CON's R1 dismantled PRO's list of inheritable contracts (all sold as heritable; personal contracts like gym memberships die), reframed the "sellers can raise prices" line as a compulsory bundle, and showed the three-children problem is not like a house because a non-transferable library cannot be liquidated. Then CON's R2 turned PRO's own A1/A2 answers into concessions: if the storefront lacking upstream rights "simply cannot call the button 'Buy,'" nothing transfers and the guarantee collapses into relabeling; if the opt-out buyer "may well pay less," PRO has adopted the priced tier with a flipped default. CON also flipped PRO's "defaults decide everything" into a privacy point against a maximal default. CON's closing anchored the vote on the motion's word "guarantee" and showed neither of PRO's outcomes is the thing on the ballot. PRO's closing did land a real counter—voiding non-transferability creates upstream bargaining pressure that disclosure does not—and CON's answer to the "tier never appeared" pressure (point-of-sale labeling untried; DRM-free stores exist) was only partial. That keeps it competitive rather than solid, but CON made the decisive clash clearer and exploited concessions more effectively.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's A1 in Rebuttal 2 [A4.5]–[A4.6]: taking PRO's own answer that a storefront without heritable upstream rights "simply cannot call the button 'Buy'" and showing this means nothing transfers—the statutory "guarantee" collapses into honest labeling in exactly the hard case, with the remainder being an unenforceable claim against a bankrupt. Paired with turning "may well pay less" into "my priced tier with the default flipped," it made PRO's mechanism look like CON's remedy under another name.</best_rebuttal>
